name: Ceramic frit (enamel) fired on glass
process: A paste of glass frit (a durable mixture of glass and ceramic particles, which act as pigments) in an organic medium is applied to the air side of the float, over the whole face or in a pattern of dots or stripes, by screen printing (through a fine mesh with a squeegee), digital printing, roller coating or curtain coating. The printed pane is dried at about 170-190 degC and then heat-strengthened or toughened: in the same heat the enamel fires and fuses to the glass. The fired layer scatters and reflects light, and a white enamel over the whole face gives an even, milky glow. Its thickness, and so its light, depends on the process and even on the screen used (for example a 68-55 W PW mesh), and two makers' 'same' RAL colour can differ.
processSources: H. R. Wilson and M. Elstner, 'Spot Landing: Determining the Light and Solar Properties of Fritted and Coated Glass', Challenging Glass 6, Delft University of Technology (2018), doi:10.7480/cgc.6.2133

mistyGlass.text: M_MistyGlass: an unlit, two-sided emissive, 'milky translucent glazing lit by the sky behind it (about 450 nits at noon: a soft pearl, not a lamp)', tint #F1F4F2, a faint cloudiness 6 m across (+/-3.5 %), brighter higher up, and the panels' horizontal seams every 1.6 m (2 cm, 15 % darker); it replaced a 64 px dot frit that 'read as a grey perforated sheet'.

carFloor.text: The car's floor: the glass instance at opacity 0.3, roughness 0.3, specular 0.5, tint (0.86, 0.90, 0.89), diffuse 0.08: 'a pale satin, so it reads as a floor you can see down through'.

asBuiltCorrection.text: The as-built misty glass is self-lit at a constant 450 nits scaled by a daylight factor. Physically it is glass that passes the sky's light and scatters it: an etched pane passes about 0.9 of it, spread over a wide cone; a white frit about 0.3, spread almost evenly; so its luminance follows the real sky behind it (and the sun's disc shows through an etched pane as a bright blur). Light should compute it from the sky and the record, never from a nits constant (principle 5: fix causes).
asBuiltCorrection.source: MuseeVision/Journal/Decisions.md, D-001 (the design is the finished museum) and D-017 (port the finished rooms; the as-built material values seed the records)

photograph: A full white frit is an even milky white by day from inside, with no bright blur of the sun; from outside it reads as white, matt enamel with a glassy sheen on the smooth face.
A dot frit reads as dots only up close; at a distance it greys the view (the as-built 64 px dot frit read as a grey perforated sheet).
